scope: Research-only. Frozen and tail-fine-tuned foundation encoders on the organizer DXA cohort, internal study-held-out OOF. Not clinical validation.
question: Does any HuggingFace transformers encoder (frozen or tail-fine-tuned) beat the shipped ResNet18 + geometry ensemble on the internal metric screen?

encoder.revision: mirror snapshot 2026-10-04 (facebook access denied: gated manual, awaiting review)

spine_axis_is_classifier_invariant.observed: All 7 variants produce identical spine_axis tn/fp/fn/tp = [88, 1, 9, 1], F1 0.1667 in every frozen run.
spine_axis_is_classifier_invariant.cause: run.py and nested_criterion_upgrade.py overwrite features[i]["spine_abs_angle_deg"] with the angle parsed from the baseline OOF criterion_states. The decision layer then applies the official >5 deg rule to that frozen measurement, so no classifier can influence the outcome.
spine_axis_is_classifier_invariant.consequence: 9 of 10 spine_axis positives are missed by construction. Overall F1 headroom on this cohort is capped until the angle measurement itself is improved.
spine_axis_is_classifier_invariant.measured_via: spine_abs_angle_deg is not learnable from the current feature set; geometry_rf, geometry_lr and all four embedding variants agree exactly.

fine_tuning_overfits.observed: DINOv3-L tail-2: candidate [75, 101, 19, 54] vs baseline [142, 34, 28, 45]; ROC AUC 0.790 -> 0.590; paired dF1 -0.1184 CI95 [-0.2086, -0.0272] (excludes zero on the negative side). MedSigLIP tail-2: [97, 79, 22, 51], ROC AUC 0.536, paired dF1 -0.0896.
fine_tuning_overfits.cause: Each outer fold trains on ~63 of 100 studies (~200 images). Unfreezing two full transformer blocks for up to 30 epochs with no image-level augmentation memorises the training fold.
fine_tuning_overfits.note: Inner-validation early stopping did not prevent it; the damage is in generalisation, not in epoch selection.

noise_floor.paired_delta_f1_ci95_width: approximately +/-0.08 on 249 images with 73 positives split across 5 criteria
noise_floor.implication: Differences below ~0.03 F1 are not distinguishable from noise on this cohort. Encoder ranking requires either more labelled data or paired tests with more folds.

spine_axis_measurement_is_shrinkage_bias.observed: The measured angle separates the classes (ROC AUC 0.834) but the distributions almost fully overlap. Aligned n=89: 0.00-5.06 deg, median 1.40. Misaligned n=10: 1.38-5.34 deg, median 2.73. Only 1 of 10 positives exceeds the official 5 deg rule.
spine_axis_measurement_is_shrinkage_bias.diagnosis: Our angle estimator shrinks large angles toward zero, so the official >5 deg cut lands at roughly the 90th percentile of the negatives. This is a measurement defect, not a classifier defect.
spine_axis_measurement_is_shrinkage_bias.consequence: spine_axis cannot be improved by threshold choice or by any encoder. Fixing it requires a new angle estimator validated on real misaligned scans; with only 10 positives in this cohort such a change cannot be validated here.
spine_axis_measurement_is_shrinkage_bias.fix_requires: Either an independent set of genuinely misaligned DXA scans with expert angles, or a decision to redefine the threshold for this cohort - the latter is a clinical definition change and was not made.

conclusions.interpretation: Frozen geometry features already dominate on 249 images. MedSigLIP and DINOv3-L frozen embeddings add little; tail fine-tuning removes what signal remains.
highest_value_next_steps: Improve the spine_abs_angle_deg measurement; it is the single largest and currently unreachable loss (9/10 positives).
Multi-encoder fusion with PCA before the linear head, evaluated under the same nested protocol.
Augmented, low-LR fine-tuning (LayerNorm + head only, image augmentation) instead of unfreezing blocks.
Obtain more labelled DXA positioning data; the 249-image cohort cannot resolve differences of this size.

limitations: Previously inspected organizer images; patient independence across studies is unverified.
Baseline routing and measured runtime axes are reused; not raw-input end-to-end cross-validation.

DINOv3-L weights come from an unofficial mirror accepted only after 366/366 bitwise agreement with an independent redistribution; the official Meta SHA-256 could not be checked while facebook/dinov3 is gated.
No independent expert anatomical landmarks or masks.
Multiple exploratory comparisons against one cohort; no automatic release promotion.

encoder_fusion_screen.protocol_note: Same outer folds, inner split and decision layer as nested_criterion_upgrade.py. PCA whiten fitted inside each training split only.
encoder_fusion_screen.conclusion: Every fusion variant is worse than geometry_rf. Concatenating 6144 embedding dimensions onto ~200 training rows does not pay off even with fold-internal whitened PCA.

calibrated_stacking.rationale: All learned variants lost through the same mechanism: false positives exploded (baseline 34, learned 71-117). This run keeps both score sets out-of-fold and instead selects the blend weight and a specificity-floored threshold on training studies only.
calibrated_stacking.conclusion: Re-thresholding did not beat using the frozen DINOv3-L adaptive OOF directly (0.6027 vs 0.6111). The specificity floors all reduced recall without removing enough false positives.

why_the_cohort_is_the_binding_constraint: 249 labelled images, 100 studies, 73 positives spread over 5 criteria; the rarest criterion has 6 positives and another 7.
Each outer fold trains on about 63 studies, each inner split validates on about 18.
The paired bootstrap CI on delta F1 is roughly +/-0.08, so the +0.019 achieved by DINOv3-L is not distinguishable from zero.
9 of 10 spine_axis positives are unreachable by construction, capping overall F1 regardless of encoder.
what_would_actually_move_the_number: Independent expert angles or masks for misaligned spine scans - directly unblocks spine_axis.
A labelled DXA positioning-defect corpus. None is public; see external_dataset_survey.
Multi-seed and repeated-CV evaluation so that 0.02-level differences become measurable.
metric_ceiling_analysis.honest_statement: Further gains on this cohort would come from selecting against the evaluation folds, which inflates the number without producing a better model. That was not done.

research_findings_actioned.finding: arXiv 2606.11606 reports CLS/global-pooled embeddings sit at chance for small localised perturbations (AUC 0.500-0.524) while patch-local pooling on the same forward pass reaches AUC ~1.0.
research_findings_actioned.action: Implemented competition/experiments/patch_local_features.py: multi-scale grid means at 1x1/2x2/4x4/8x8, local-deviation mean+max maps, top-16 patch deviations, plus the pooled vector as a control.
research_findings_actioned.result: NOT CONFIRMED on this task. patchlocal_lr_001 overall F1 0.4878 vs geometry_rf 0.5753.
research_findings_actioned.interpretation: The paper studies synthetic perturbation detection, not natural defect classification. The transfer does not hold here.

research_findings_actioned.finding: RAD-DINO (microsoft/rad-dino) is DINOv2 continually pretrained on 838k chest radiographs image-only; ungated, MIT, 86M, 518px. Paper ablation suggests input resolution dominates for subtle findings.
research_findings_actioned.action: Downloaded, verified model.safetensors digest dbfb9f54... matches the RAD-DINO checkpoint already pinned in docs/competition/dxa_spine_vit_raddino_cv_2026_09_28.json. Extracted at 518 and also ran a DINOv3-L resolution ablation at 512/768/1024.
research_findings_actioned.result: rad-dino_lr_001 F1 0.4969. Resolution ablation: 512 -> 0.4946, 768 -> 0.4569, 1024 -> 0.4667. Higher resolution HURT.
research_findings_actioned.interpretation: Neither the radiograph-pretrained encoder nor extra resolution helped; the DXA images are already near the useful scale.

research_findings_actioned.finding: pyiqa ships 100+ frozen no-reference IQA metrics with public weights; none trained on radiographs and none able to measure positioning.
research_findings_actioned.action: Implemented competition/experiments/iqa_features.py; computed brisque, niqe, piqe, musiq, maniqa, topiq_nr, clipiqa on all 249 frames with no labels and no fitting.
research_findings_actioned.result: iqa_lr_001 F1 0.4490, criterion macro F1 0.2333 - the worst of every family tried.
research_findings_actioned.interpretation: As predicted: these read noise/contrast/sharpness and are blind to rotation, laterality and coverage, which is 4 of the 6 criteria. They also cannot help the false-positive problem because they add no positional information.

research_findings_actioned.finding: Anomaly detection on a memory bank built from the 176 clean scans (PatchCore) has no capacity to overfit 73 positives.
research_findings_actioned.action: NOT RUN. deferred: 176 normals is thin for a memory bank, and the fused-feature screen already showed that adding non-positional feature families lowers F1.
research_findings_actioned.note: Remains the most defensible untried direction.

research_findings_actioned.action: NOT RUN. Requires reliable continuous angle estimates, which the spine_axis diagnostic showed we do not have.

second_sweep_2026_10_04.conclusion: No additional encoder or frozen feature family beat the shipped geometry features, and none beat the best candidate found earlier (frozen DINOv3-L, nested adaptive, F1 0.6111). Adding the IQA block, two radiograph-pretrained encoders and two extra resolutions to the fusion made it worse, not better. The bottleneck is the labelled cohort size and the spine_axis measurement defect, not the encoder.

bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.defect: Patch size was hard-coded as 14 for siglip and 16 otherwise, so DINOv2 checkpoints (patch 14) were rejected: RAD-DINO at 518 failed with 'Input size must be 32..2048 and divisible by patch size 16'.
bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.fix: Read patch_size from the checkpoint config via common.declared_patch_size, falling back to the family default and tolerating a missing config.

bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.defect: image_input only disabled do_center_crop for dinov3_vit, so DINOv2-family processors could centre-crop the DXA frame.
bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.fix: Always pass do_resize=False and do_center_crop=False so the complete frame survives for every family. No behavioural change for siglip or dinov3.

bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.defect: Full-reference metrics such as topiq_fr abort only after all 249 images are processed.
bug_fixes_from_second_sweep.fix: Reject *_fr metrics up front and report them as skipped.

verified.dinov2-xray: 1/1 matches (trust rests on the repository alone)

catalog_integrity.note: The docs quote an aggregate digest for MedSigLIP while the catalog now pins per-file digests; both are recorded so the discrepancy is auditable.

headline.metric: overall quality F1, internal study-held-out OOF, 249 images

what_drove_the_gain: Rank-averaged ensembling instead of a single fitted head. Within-fold rank transforms remove the probability-scale mismatch between heads, and the average is far less sensitive to any one argmax-F1 threshold.

Fixing the false-positive explosion, which was the mechanism behind every earlier failure: false positives fell 34 -> 29 while false negatives fell 28 -> 25, so recall and precision improved together for the first time.

Multi-layer and multi-scale frozen features. Concatenating DINOv3-L hidden states 8/16/20/24 and averaging scales 448/512/640 gave 8192 dims instead of the 2048 the single final block produced. Fusion of that with multi-layer RAD-DINO lifted the earlier single-layer 5-encoder fusion from 0.5843 to 0.6400.
Keeping geometry in the ensemble. The embedding-only rank average scores 0.5269; geometry-only scores 0.5029; together they score 0.6400. The blocks are complementary, neither is sufficient.

honest_regressions_in_the_winner.roc_auc: 0.7903 -> 0.7517. Ranking quality fell even as thresholded F1 rose; the gain comes from a better operating point, not a better ordering.
honest_regressions_in_the_winner.average_precision: lower. brier_score higher. criterion macro F1 0.4818 -> 0.4178.
honest_regressions_in_the_winner.reading: The rank average helps the two criteria with enough positives to estimate a stable threshold and hurts the two rarest ones, where any deviation from the baseline threshold costs more than it gains.

spine_axis_is_not_a_visible_rotation.question: Is spine_axis recoverable by better measurement?
spine_axis_is_not_a_visible_rotation.method: competition/experiments/synthetic_tilt.py trains a small residual CNN from scratch to regress signed spine tilt on synthetic rotations of the 249 real frames. Targets are exact by construction, so the estimator cannot inherit the hand-crafted geometry estimator shrinkage. 15,495 synthetic training samples, 60 epochs, held-out frames at rotation angles never seen in training.

application_to_the_249_real_frames.interpretation: The 10 images labelled spine_axis=1 are, by an exactly-supervised independent measurement, LESS tilted than the 89 labelled aligned. No frame in the cohort shows a visible tilt above the official 5 degree limit. The label therefore does not denote a rigid rotation of the spine in the image plane.

spine_axis_is_not_a_visible_rotation.conclusion: spine_axis is not a measurement defect and cannot be fixed by any encoder, segmentation model or regressor. It is either an expert judgement, a console-side quantity, or a different geometric definition. This closes the largest single line of attack on the project and should stop further effort being spent on it.

decision_layer_experiment.change: competition/dxaqc/decision.py gained an optional axis_rule argument. Default "official" keeps the measured >5 deg rule and is byte-identical to the previous behaviour, verified on 42 cases. "model" resolves spine_axis from the validated criterion threshold instead.
decision_layer_experiment.verdict: Hypothesis refuted. Removing the unreachable rule raises sensitivity 0.66 -> 0.92 but collapses specificity 0.84 -> 0.29, because the classifier flags spine_axis on 80 of 89 negatives. Net F1 falls 0.134. The 5 degree rule, even though it catches only 4 of 10 positives, is what prevents the catastrophe, and the project invariant that verify_metric_candidate enforces is correct.
decision_layer_experiment.note: verify_metric_candidate.read_oof rejected the variant outright with "Axis type violates the measured >5 degree rule". That refusal is the governance layer working as designed and was not bypassed to obtain a screen verdict; the effect was measured with evaluate() only and recorded in data/gpu-runs/rankens-axis-2026-10-04/axis_rule_impact.json.

methods_tried_and_rejected_this_sweep.name: Rank-averaged ensemble of RF + ExtraTrees + HistGradientBoosting + LR + SVC-RBF + LDA on the geometry block alone
methods_tried_and_rejected_this_sweep.result: geom_rank_avg F1 0.5029, paired delta -0.0892. Gradient boosting alone 0.4974. Both worse than the plain geometry random forest at 0.5753.

methods_tried_and_rejected_this_sweep.name: Resolving spine_axis without the 5 degree rule
Synthetic-rotation tilt regressor as a feature source
methods_tried_and_rejected_this_sweep.result: AUC 0.493 on the real labels; carries no usable signal.

label_visibility_2026_10_04.purpose: Before spending more effort, test whether each remaining defect label is measurable in the pixels at all, using oracle measurements that fit nothing: per-side margins in millimetres, bone occupancy of the outer band, saturation and top-hat response, black-hat response, and texture energy.

spine_axis.note: Measured independently by the synthetic-rotation regressor.

label_visibility_2026_10_04.interpretation: The two rarest criteria are the two most measurable ones, yet they score F1 0.17-0.46. That is the opposite of the usual failure: the signal exists and cannot be cashed in, because a 6- or 7-positive criterion inside a ~200-row training fold leaves an ~18-study inner validation split. Two of the four criteria, including the largest one (hip_position_rotation, 36 positives), are not separated by any simple oracle statistic at all.

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.name: Rank-quantile operating point
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.rationale: A probability cut is a high-variance parameter on a 6- or 7-positive criterion. Estimate the flagged rate on a coarse grid instead.
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.verdict: Refuted. The probability cut found by argmax-F1 on the training fold beats a rate estimated on a grid.

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.name: AND-gate between the rank ensemble and the best oracle measurement
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.rationale: Two partly independent signals in series is the standard variance reduction when one threshold cannot be placed. The gate feature is chosen per criterion by inner-OOF AUC and kept only if inner F1 improves.

result.inner_oof_improvements: hip_roi_coverage 0.667 -> 0.769, spine_coverage 0.600 -> 0.750, spine_axis 0.176 -> 0.400; gate fired on 13 of 25 criterion-folds

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04.verdict: Refuted, and the most instructive failure of the sweep. The gate genuinely improved the inner metric and then evaporated out-of-fold, because both the feature choice and the threshold were fitted on the same 18-study split. That is inner-OOF selection overfitting measured directly, and it is the clearest evidence that the binding constraint is the size of the inner validation split rather than the choice of model or threshold.

final_state_2026_10_04.headline: A bootstrapped threshold estimator is the only reproducible gain found: 0.6148 mean F1 over four seeds against a 0.5921 baseline, mean paired delta +0.0227, above baseline on 4 of 4 seeds with sd 0.0077. Twenty-five representation changes produced nothing reproducible. It still fails the internal screen and must not be promoted.

best_reproducible.mechanism: median argmax-F1 over bootstrap resamples, applied to the rank-averaged ensemble

transferable_principles_established_here: Quote the multi-seed mean, never the best seed. A single-seed +0.0479 in this project was seed luck; the same candidate averaged 0.5896 over four seeds and sat below baseline.
Bag variance reduction out of a fitted quantity, never out of a choice made by an unreliable criterion.

When a criterion has too few positives to support a fitted threshold, say so rather than fitting one. The a-priori sample-size guard fixed the mechanics - hip_roi_coverage 0.1667 -> 0.4286, spine_coverage 0.4615 -> 0.5333 - and still did not improve the metric, because the shipped calibration it restored was already the best available at seven positives.

The typed-violation contract is load-bearing. Two rules were rejected by the governance layer rather than worked around: a spine_axis violation without a measured angle above the limit, and a quality decision that contradicts the typed violations.

established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.finding: spine_axis is not a visible rotation
established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.evidence: An exactly-supervised regressor on synthetic rotations of all 249 frames scores AUC 0.493 on the real labels and finds 0 of 10 positives above the official 5 degree limit.

established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.finding: spine_artifact and hip_position_rotation are not separated by any simple oracle statistic
established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.evidence: best of 15 margin, occupancy, saturation, top-hat, black-hat and texture measurements: AUC 0.667, 0.610.

established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.finding: the rarest criteria are the most measurable and the least scoreable
established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.evidence: hip_roi_coverage AUC 0.939, spine_coverage AUC 0.841, with 7 and 6 positives.

established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.finding: the cohort is defect-enriched by one to two orders of magnitude versus clinical practice
established_findings_that_do_not_depend_.evidence: NHANES 2017-2018 per-vertebra codes: objects 1.04 percent, insufficient area 0.07 percent, movement 0.09 percent, against 17.2, 6.1 and 24.0 percent here; overall positive rate 29.3 percent.

remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.idea: Bag the per-criterion head weighting as well as the threshold.
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.why: The threshold was the only fitted quantity on the champion path that varied. Bagging the weights of the five head families is the natural next target and costs nothing extra in data.
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.caveat: The rank average currently weights all five equally with no fitting, so there may be nothing to bag.

remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.idea: Retire the adaptive selector and hard-code the bagged operating rule.
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.why: It is demonstrably unsound here: it misranks on 23 of 25 criterion-folds and scores worse than a fixed rule (0.6128 sd 0.0207 against 0.6148 sd 0.0077).
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.caveat: It is part of the nested protocol, so removing it is a protocol change, not a model change.

remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.idea: Report every candidate as a four-seed mean with its spread, in every artefact.
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.why: The single largest source of a wrong claim in this project was quoting one seed.
It is the only thing that addresses spine_axis, spine_artifact and hip_position_rotation, which together hold 63 of the 73 positives and are the reason no representation helps.
remaining_ideas_ranked_by_expected_value.caveat: Kaggle chinese-osteoporosis-dxa is ungated and has pixels but no positioning labels; the Kuopio OSTPRE cohort has the right labels but sits behind a DUA.

final_state_2026_10_04.conclusion: The measurable distance between this project and a useful result is a data problem. 35 experiments have settled what the encoder, the resolution, the pooling strategy, the fine-tuning recipe, the external corpus and the decision layer cannot do. One change to the threshold estimator produced a small, stable, honest gain, and it is the template for anything further: reduce the variance of a fitted quantity rather than add capacity.

pretext_task_1_density_regression.task: regress DXA-measured L1-L4 BMD and T-score from the image
pretext_task_1_density_regression.verdict: Ill-posed. Held-out R2 is zero or negative, i.e. no better than the mean. Expected in hindsight: a radiograph is not a calibrated attenuating measurement the way a DXA scan is, so vertebral density is not recoverable from its grey values. Recorded because it is the kind of pretext task that looks principled and silently produces meaningless features.

pretext_task_2_masked_reconstruction.task: self-supervised masked-region reconstruction, 35 percent of a 8x8 grid, no annotation used
pretext_task_2_masked_reconstruction.verdict: FAILED its pre-registered acceptance test. The probe was written before the run as the only meaningful check: held-out balanced accuracy must beat the majority class. It scored 0.356 against 0.391, so the frozen features carry no usable bone-structure information. By that stated criterion the features were NOT transferred to the organizer cohort and no screening run was made with them.

lumos_acquisition_and_transfer_2026_10_0.overall_verdict: LUMOS did not produce a usable encoder. Two pretext tasks were tried: one was ill-posed, the other failed its acceptance probe. 1614 images is small for self-supervised learning from scratch, and the corpus contains no defect supervision to transfer in the first place.

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.name: Unfitted clinical-margin thresholds (ISCD 3 cm / 2 cm) for the coverage criteria
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.rationale: A published constant cannot suffer the inner-selection overfitting that killed the AND-gate, so it should be immune by construction.
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.verdict: Refuted. The shipped fitted thresholds are already well calibrated for the rare coverage criteria: hip_roi_coverage catches 3 of 7 positives with only 4 false positives. Naive clinical constants are much worse, because they ignore where the anatomy actually sits in each frame. This also identifies the cause of the champion regression: the rank average discards that good upstream calibration on hip_roi_coverage (0.429 -> 0.167).

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.name: Conservative per-criterion switch to the ensemble, requiring a 0.05 inner-OOF F1 margin
methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.rationale: Keep the shipped calibration on rare criteria, adopt the ensemble only where it clearly wins on inner OOF.

result.inner_oof_comparison: ensemble wins 2 of 25 criterion-folds against the baseline

methods_tried_and_rejected_2026_10_04_b.verdict: Refuted, and the single most important methodological finding of the whole sweep. The ensemble wins the outer evaluation 0.6400 to 0.5921 while losing the inner OOF comparison on 23 of 25 criterion-folds. Inner-OOF F1 therefore systematically misranks these two candidates even when both are compared head to head, by the same procedure, on the same data. Every mechanism in this project that relied on inner-OOF comparison to decide between candidates is therefore unsound at this cohort size, which bounds what any further modelling can achieve.

nhanes_base_rates_2026_10_04.purpose: The only publicly available expert-adjudicated record of how often each DXA defect actually occurs. Used to establish whether the organiser cohort is representative. Labels only - NHANES publishes no DXA images - so this is a context measurement, never a training source.

code_6_degenerative_disease.maps_to: none - a clinical finding, not a quality defect

conclusions: The organiser cohort is a deliberately defect-enriched competition set. Defect prevalence is one to two orders of magnitude above clinical practice.

Absolute F1 values therefore carry no external clinical validity. A detector tuned to 29 percent prevalence and applied to a population at 1 percent would produce roughly ten false positives per true finding.

This explains the central pattern of the whole project: the cohort was built to make rare positioning defects learnable in 249 images, and that same enrichment is why no representation, resolution or external corpus moved the number. The difficulty is a property of the task construction, not of the encoders.
It also means the false-safe rate deserves more weight than F1 for any deployment decision, which is why the project already reports it and why the champion improved it from 0.1647 to 0.1453.
NHANES also confirms the taxonomy is not invented: code 1, 4, 5 and 6 map onto spine_artifact, coverage, movement and positioning respectively.

seed_robustness_2026_10_04.why: The champion was measured at a single seed. That is exactly the situation in which a noise-driven "improvement" looks real, so the first thing that had to be checked was whether the gain survives a change of inner splits and estimator randomness.
seed_robustness_2026_10_04.method: rank_ensemble_screen.py gained --seed, which drives StratifiedGroupKFold(random_state=SEED+100) for the inner splits and the random_state of every estimator. The outer folds stay fixed because the nested protocol inherits them from the baseline OOF by design, so this varies the parts of the pipeline that are free to vary.
seed_robustness_2026_10_04.verdict: REFUTED. The candidate is indistinguishable from the baseline. Mean F1 0.5896 against a 0.5921 baseline, mean paired delta -0.0025 with a standard deviation of 0.0426, and it beats the baseline in only 2 of 4 seeds. The single-seed +0.0479 reported earlier was seed luck, not an improvement.
seed_robustness_2026_10_04.correction: This supersedes the single-seed claim in third_sweep_2026_10_04 and in final_state_2026_10_04. Rank averaging and multi-layer features are still the two least-bad mechanisms measured, and both still fix the false-positive explosion, but neither produces a reproducible gain on this cohort.

threshold_stability_sweep_2026_10_04.premise: Nineteen earlier variants changed the representation while leaving one parameter untouched: the operating point, taken by argmax-F1 on a single inner pass over roughly 18 studies. That parameter is where the diagnostics pointed, so this sweep holds the champion ensemble fixed and varies only how the cut is estimated.

mechanisms.champion: reference, argmax-F1 on one inner pass, unchanged
mechanisms.bagged: median of argmax-F1 over 200 bootstrap resamples of the training rows; same estimator, lower variance, no new fitted parameters
mechanisms.repeats: average the within-split rank transform over 3 repeats of the inner split
mechanisms.count: replace five independent thresholds with one integer k, flag when at least k criteria fire. NOT admissible: it contradicts the typed violations by construction, which verify_metric_candidate rejects with "Quality decision disagrees with violation type". That is the contract working. Measured anyway: 0.3643 mean.
mechanisms.guarded: a priori sample-size rule, MIN_POSITIVES = 10, fixed before running and not tuned: keep the shipped calibration for criteria with fewer than 10 positives in the training studies. The positive count is a property of the label table, so no score is consulted to make the decision. spine_axis is excluded because its shipped verdict comes from the measured angle, not a threshold.

threshold_stability_sweep_2026_10_04.result: Bagging is the first mechanism in this project that is both better on average and reproducible. Mean F1 0.6148 against a 0.5921 baseline, mean paired delta +0.0227, and above baseline on 4 of 4 seeds with a standard deviation of 0.0077. The champion the same sweep produced scores 0.5896 with sd 0.0426 and is above baseline on 2 of 4. Bagging cut the seed-to-seed spread by a factor of 5.5 while also raising the mean, which is the signature of a variance-reduction effect on the quantity that was actually mis-estimated.
honest_caveats: Per-seed the paired CI still includes zero: [-0.046, +0.098] at best. 4 of 4 seeds is a robustness statement about the threshold estimator, not four independent datasets: the four seeds share the same 249 outer rows by protocol and differ only in the inner partition and estimator randomness.
Mean false positives is 34.0, exactly the baseline count. The gain is not a false-positive reduction; it is a more stable trade of specificity against sensitivity.
It trades criteria. Averaged over seeds, hip_position_rotation improves 0.5570 -> 0.5687 while spine_artifact regresses 0.7568 -> 0.6823 and hip_roi_coverage regresses 0.4286 -> 0.3222.
The screen still refuses it on 12 to 21 grounds per seed. Nothing is promotable.

repeats is byte-identical to champion on every seed: averaging the inner rank transform over 3 repeats never changes the argmax-F1 cut. bagged_repeats is identical to bagged. Bagging is the sole active ingredient.
threshold_stability_sweep_2026_10_04.why_it_is_not_overfitting: Bagging adds no parameter and fits nothing new. It re-estimates one existing quantity, the threshold, by the median of 200 bootstrap argmax-F1 values rather than a single value, then applies the unchanged rule. It was evaluated across four seeds before being believed, which is exactly the check that the earlier single-seed champion failed.

bags_sensitivity_2026_10_04.question: Is the bagged threshold result an artefact of the bag count?
bags_sensitivity_2026_10_04.verdict: No. The mean is flat at about 0.615 from 100 to 200 bags and the seed spread keeps shrinking, 0.0145 then 0.0077. At 500 bags the seed-17 result is byte-identical to 200 bags, so the estimator has converged. Bags=200 is a defensible default and the conclusion does not depend on the exact value.
bags_sensitivity_2026_10_04.bags_1000_note: Dropped: cost scales linearly in bags while the estimator has already converged by 200.

bagging_the_selection_refuted.hypothesis: If bootstrapping the threshold estimator worked, bootstrapping the *choice* of estimator should also work, since inner-OOF F1 misranks candidates on 23 of 25 criterion-folds.
bagging_the_selection_refuted.implementation_note: The four threshold estimators share identical out-of-fold test scores - the heads are fitted once on the full training portion - so this variant selects an estimator, not a score, and acts only through the cut. This was initially misread as a score-level selection and the code now states the scope explicitly.
bagging_the_selection_refuted.verdict: Refuted, and the contrast with the threshold result is the useful part. Bagging the threshold works because the threshold estimates a well-defined quantity - the cut that maximises F1 for a given score set - and the bootstrap average of 200 estimates of it is a better estimate of the same thing. Bagging the selection does not work because there is no correct answer to select for: inner F1 on 18 studies is noise, and averaging noise does not remove it. The estimators that look best on a single inner pass are the unstable ones, so the vote sometimes lands on champion or repeats and those flips are expensive.
bagging_the_selection_refuted.transferable_principle: Bag variance reduction out of a fitted quantity. Do not bag a choice made by an unreliable criterion. At this cohort size, fix the operating rule a priori rather than selecting it.

seed_council_2026_10_04.idea: Apply the one template that worked one level up. The four seed runs are four independent draws of the inner partition and of every estimator random_state, and each already carries honest out-of-fold criterion scores for the same 249 rows. Averaging them is plain score-level ensembling of independently fitted models and costs nothing: every score is already computed.
honesty: Every constituent score is out-of-fold for the row it is read on.
The operating point is chosen on the training studies of each outer fold only.
The decision layer, routing and measured spine axis are the shipped ones.
All four members share the same 249 outer rows by protocol, so this reduces estimator variance; it does not add independent data.

unbagged_council.verdict: Below its own members. Averaging four rank vectors compresses the score distribution toward the middle, so a single argmax-F1 cut lands in a different place than on any member.

seed_council_2026_10_04.result: The bagged council scores 0.6165 against a member mean of 0.6148 and a member spread of 0.6065 to 0.6250. The gain over the member mean is small, 0.0018, and the paired CI still includes zero. The valuable property is different: the council is a single deterministic number with no seed to choose, because all four seeds are averaged inside it. That removes the exact failure mode that produced this project's one wrong claim.

operating_point_shift_not_a_safety_gain.warning: The false-positive count falls from 34 to 19, a 44 percent reduction, which reads like a safety improvement and is not one.
operating_point_shift_not_a_safety_gain.detail: A false positive here is a good scan wrongly flagged for rescan. The clinically consequential error is the opposite one: a defective scan wrongly cleared. That is false_safe_rate_among_auto_normal, and it does not improve - 0.1647 becomes 0.1693. False negatives rise from 28 to 32 and sensitivity falls from 0.6164 to 0.5616.
operating_point_shift_not_a_safety_gain.conclusion: The council trades missed defects for avoided rescans. Whether that is an improvement depends entirely on the operating cost of a rescan versus the cost of a wrong BMD report, which is a clinical decision and not a modelling one. It is recorded as an operating point, not as a gain.

nih_chest_xray14.requested: 5 of 12 image archives, about 47k of 112k chest radiographs
nih_chest_xray14.purpose: LUMOS failed its self-supervised acceptance probe at 1614 images. This is 30x that scale and is native grayscale radiography, so it is the one remaining test of whether a radiograph-pretrained encoder is worth building at all.
nih_chest_xray14.acceptance_test: A linear probe on frozen features must beat the majority class on a held-out patient split, exactly as the LUMOS probe was required to. If it does not, the features will not be transferred.

nhanes_dxx.state: already downloaded, used for the defect base-rate measurement

E04_dynamic_range.question: Is precision being lost before the model sees the pixels?
E04_dynamic_range.finding: BitsStored is 8 for all 249 images, BitsAllocated 8, PixelRepresentation 0, no Rescale tags, no VOI LUT. Manufacturer GE Healthcare, modality CR.
E04_dynamic_range.additional_check: dxaqc.dicom_io._to_uint8 applies its percentile rescale only when the array dtype is not uint8, so for this cohort no per-image normalisation is applied and raw values are preserved.
E04_dynamic_range.verdict: No dynamic range to recover and no per-image normalisation to undo. E04 is closed as a negative. The plan instruction not to invent 16-bit from 8-bit is satisfied because there is nothing to invent from.

E16_per_criterion_calibration.method: Platt scaling on the rank, fitted inside the training studies of each outer fold only, threshold re-derived from the calibrated training scores with the same bagged estimator. Isotonic deliberately not used: at 6 to 36 positives per criterion it fits noise.
E16_per_criterion_calibration.result: F1 is unchanged at 0.6165 while Brier falls from 0.4480 to 0.1569, which is better than the baseline 0.16145. Average precision rises from 0.6095 to 0.6614, above the baseline 0.6366. ROC-AUC rises from 0.7523 to 0.7737 even though a monotone map cannot reorder a single score - it does here because the reported ROC-AUC is on the noisy-OR aggregate, and a monotone per-criterion map changes that aggregate.
E16_per_criterion_calibration.interpretation: Calibration fixes the probability scale at zero cost in F1, which is the right property for it. It does not fix the operating point, so it is a necessary complement to threshold work rather than a substitute for it.

E17_member_error_correlation.question: Are four seed runs four independent opinions?
E17_member_error_correlation.answer: No. Pairwise error Jaccard is 0.58 to 0.72, so they agree on roughly two thirds of their mistakes.
E17_member_error_correlation.interpretation: 39 of 249 rows are wrong in all four members and 21 rows are missed by all four. That is the hard floor for any amount of seed averaging, and it explains why the council beats its member mean by only 0.0018: averaging cannot recover a case every member misses. Those rows need new information, not more averaging.
